cards.explanation: The answer is True. Asa, the new king of Judah, did what was good and right in the eyes of the LORD his God (2 Chronicles 14:2). That's how the writer sums him up before telling us what he did. Most of us would need a few extra paragraphs to explain ourselves, friends.

The answer is to seek the LORD and keep His law. Asa commanded the people of Judah "…to seek the LORD, the God of their fathers, and to observe the law and the commandments." (2 Chronicles 14:4). Notice he doesn't just clear things out and walk away. He points the people toward the LORD. Clearing the shelf is half the job, friends, and filling it with the right thing is the other half.

The word is fortified. "Because the land was at peace, Asa built fortified cities in Judah." (2 Chronicles 14:6). Peace is the time he uses to build. That's like fixing the roof on a sunny day, friends, and I bet nobody in Judah complained about it.

The word is rest. "…the LORD had given him rest." (2 Chronicles 14:6). Asa says the same thing to the people: "…He has given us rest on every side." (2 Chronicles 14:7). Rest is a gift here, and the text says who gave it. That's the kind of gift I'd happily unwrap twice, bakers.

The answer is False. Asa tells Judah, "The land is still ours because we have sought the LORD our God." (2 Chronicles 14:7). He doesn't brag about the army. He says the LORD has given them rest on every side. I'd say the king knows exactly where the credit goes, friends.

The answer is that he cries out to the LORD his God. "Then Asa cried out to the LORD his God…" (2 Chronicles 14:11). He has marched out and lined up in battle formation, and a million men are in front of him. Right there in the valley, he prays. That's a good lesson for me, bakers, because at a hard moment I'm more likely to stare at the ceiling.

The answer is True. Asa prays, "O LORD, You are our God. Do not let a mere mortal prevail against You." (2 Chronicles 14:11). He's facing Zerah the Cushite, who leads that huge army. Asa speaks to the LORD plainly and gets right to it, friends.

The answer is the LORD their God. Asa prays, "Help us, O LORD our God, for we rely on You…" He also says, "…there is no one besides You to help the powerless against the mighty." (2 Chronicles 14:11). The people are lined up in the valley with their weapons, friends, but the prayer rests on the LORD.

The answer is that the LORD strikes them down and they flee. "So the LORD struck down the Cushites before Asa and Judah, and the Cushites fled." (2 Chronicles 14:12). The prayer ends and the LORD acts right away in the text. A million men, friends, and the LORD is the one who handles it.

The answer is False. "The Cushites fell and could not recover, for they were crushed before the LORD and His army." (2 Chronicles 14:13). Nobody is coming back for round two, friends. After the chase to Gerar, the text turns to Judah's plunder.

The word is terror. The verse says, "…the terror of the LORD had fallen upon them." That's why Judah attacked all the cities around Gerar and plundered them, since there was much plunder there (2 Chronicles 14:14). I'd say that's a whole lot of fear landing at once, bakers.
